are you actually comparing a sub $30 pen to a Parker Duofold (that's what model that pen looks like)? Care to compare apples to Ostriches next?

Why yes, yes I am. Just as I compared my Duofold to my Montblanc Agatha Christie when I got it... price differential doesn't inhibit comparisons IMO, just provides the excuse on the other end of the user experience. Maybe (the Duofold beat the Montblanc in every way but price).

Price differentials don't really prohibit comparisons, no. But a large enough difference should prohibit the expectation that two items provide equal experiences. At least at this level.

Obviously, the price difference between a MB 149 and a Pelikan M1000 should not be a factor in expectations of their comparable experience. Similarly, a TWSBI 580 and Sheaffer 300 should also be comparable. But things like gold nibs, better materials, etc., definitely mean a different experience. Note I didn't say better, just different.

To some it may be better to have a gold nib or celluloid body, or integrated filling system, whatever. But to just randomly compare two pens from wildly different market segments serves no purpose other than to reinforce (surprise, surprise) that the person doing the comparing likes the much more expensive pen- which in all likelihood features things the other pen doesn't even offer, that no pen of that price tier offers- more.
